chapter: Gambling, Cab's small groups and Havana
title: The four-piece Cab Jivers in Havana and Cuban musicians
summary: Playing the Montmartre in Havana, they met musicians such as Candito, Filiberto Sanchez and Chapottin.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Four, right. That was when we played in Cuba, in Havana, Cuba at the Monmartre.
Yeah, we stayed toger for about a year with those four pieces.
The four pieces -- yeah, they were the Small Cab Jivers.
Yeah, and we'd go to places like the Monmartre, that night spot in Havana, Cuba, and we would be augmented by the Cuban band.
Do you have anything to say about those band in those days? Remember that band in Havana? And some of the guys we met? Remember Bruno?
Oh yeah, I remember Bruno, and I remember Candito and I met down there.
Candifo was a great trumpet player.

Yeah, and a great congo player.. But I met Candifo down there, and he took me to the airport and he couldn't speak any English and I couldn't speak any Spanish, and how we understood each other I don't know, but we did and we got to the airport and said goodbye to each other, and we rode all the way out there without saying a word.
I remember once, Cab tried to bring him back, before we ever got here, and they wouldn't let him leave.
They wouldn't let him leave Cuba at that time -- that's right. And, also, what was that bass player who was with the police band -- he later on came.
Oh, yes ... I remember his name, but I can't recall it now.

But there was a guy there who was also in the police band named Filiberto Sanchez that they all respected; I mean, all of the bongo players and congo players respected him, but he couldn't leave because he was on the police force and he had a big family. But he was very much respected by all the fellows around there, and that's where I met Migelito Valdez' brother -- Daddio? Remember Daddio? Pozo's
And Chino's brother who played the violin?
Played the violin. And the trumpet player over there, Chapartine.
Chapartine, the bass player. Yeah. He lives in Spain now, you know.
Yeah, he used to always come to New York and carry your umbrella, remember that?
